title: Shadow of the Tomb Raider, Lara standing, frames 24-35 (plays)
images: This build: network every 4th frame, split over 4 frames
Reference: network every frame (about 3x the cost)
intro: Shadow of the Tomb Raider. Lara standing in the night market, the camera moving slowly. Twelve frames. Look at the arms and the torso: their lighting should stay as steady as in the reference, without a wobble in a 4-frame rhythm. Open "About these pictures" for the setup and numbers.
about:
Setup

Shadow of the Tomb Raider: a captured game clip, 4K output, upscaler Balanced (render 2258x1270), NR at 0.75 scale. Same settings as the 0.0.9-split.1 preview (its default preset, 1 pass; Stellar Blade with its own reuse settings: no revealed-background fill, Snap on). Every picture then goes through FSR 4 Lite lossy (4.1.2l-lossy, the 2026-11-19 build) at 4K.

What to look at

Lara standing in the night market, the camera moving slowly. Twelve frames. Look at the arms and the torso: their lighting should stay as steady as in the reference, without a wobble in a 4-frame rhythm.

Numbers

Against the reference (PSNR, whole 4K frame): this build 44.7 dB on frames 24-35, NR off 35.9 dB; over the whole clip 44.4 vs 36.2 dB. Least close frame of the clip: frame 10, 42.3 dB.

Notes

Frames from captured game clips, run through the plugin's own runtime in a test harness (deterministic, one run each); the display mapping is ours (x/(1+x), gamma 1/2.2), not the game's tone mapping; no UI. Built on DLSSNR-AMD (TheAutomatic and contributors) and the RDNA3 ports by mauri870 and hedonemaeda. Not affiliated with, endorsed by or supported by NVIDIA or AMD.
